subject: chemistry
title: Organic Reactions Adventure: Equations, Polymers, Esters
welcome_lead: Today you'll balance combustion, make a polymer and an ester.
meta_desc: GCSE Chemistry — balanced combustion equations, addition polymerisation of ethene to poly(ethene), and ester formation.
final_note: You learned how to balance combustion, how poly(ethene) is made, and how esters form from alcohols and acids.

walkthroughs.body_html:
CH4 + O2 → CO2 + H2O — but the atoms don't yet balance.

Balance H first: put a 2 in front of H2O. Now there are 4 O on the right and 2 on the left, so put a 2 in front of O2.

Final: CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O. Check: 1 C, 4 H, 4 O each side. ✓

Many ethene monomers link together. The C=C bond opens and the carbons join end to end.

n C2H4 → −[CH2−CH2]−n. Only one product, no atoms lost — that's addition polymerisation.

Alcohol + carboxylic acid (with an acid catalyst) → ester + water.

Ethanol + ethanoic acid → ethyl ethanoate + water. Esters smell sweet and fruity — pear drops, nail polish remover, glue.

CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O
2CH4 + O2 → 2CO2 + H2O
CH4 + 3O2 → CO2 + 2H2O

mcqs.q: Addition polymerisation needs which monomer feature?
options: A C=C double bond
An −OH group
A −COOH group
A benzene ring

mcqs.q: How do alkenes typically react with bromine?
options: The alkene polymerises with bromine to form a long chain.
Bromine substitutes for a hydrogen on the alkene, releasing HBr.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.
By electrophilic addition — bromine adds across the double bond to form a dibromoalkane.

mcqs.q: What is different between two isotopes of the same element?
options: A strong acid is one that has been heated to higher temperature.
Isotopes have different numbers of electrons, which is why their mass differs.
They have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a strong acid and a concentrated acid?
options: Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.
Strong and concentrated mean the same thing for acids.
A strong acid fully dissociates in water; a concentrated acid has a high amount of acid per volume — these are independent properties.
A strong acid is one that has been heated to higher temperature.
